title: Rift MCP surface
description: JSON values accepted and returned by the Rift MCP server. Each definition carries the Protobuf identity used after `rift mcp` decodes the request.

rift:entryPoints.description: The internal connection stream establishes the gRPC context used by later calls. Tools map MCP request and result JSON to Rift service methods: the typed result rides `structuredContent` against the tool's declared output schema, mirrored as one canonical-JSON `text` block, and a refusal is such a result — never `isError`. `ErrorData` travels as the JSON-RPC error object's `data` with code -32000. The MCP process queues those calls and issues one application RPC at a time; a cancelled queued call is dropped, and a cancelled running change completes or rolls back whole. Each resource entry maps one URI family to the types that carry it.

search.description: Searches symbols, nodes, and files in the session projection.

match.description: Finds literal, regular-expression, or structural matches.

edit.description: Applies and validates an atomic edit set, and records the result in the changeset.

patch.description: Applies a unified diff, and records the result in the changeset.

rewrite.description: Applies replacements for every match of one query. The cardinality is checked before expansion, so a pattern that matches more places than intended refuses instead of rewriting them.

rename.description: Changes what a declaration is called and rewrites every reference that names it. The adapter checks spelling, collisions, and binding changes. A reference outside the scope refuses the whole operation.

move.description: Moves a declaration or file to another container or path and updates the imports and references that reach it.

delete.description: Removes a declaration. Without a policy this is a mechanical removal that analyses no references. With one, the adapter classifies every remaining use, applies the stated disposition, and refuses when reference coverage is incomplete.

change_signature.description: Changes the shape of a callable and propagates it to callers, overrides, and implementations. Unlike a rename, it rewrites argument lists, so it commonly raises a `behavior_unknown` confirmation.

apply.description: Resolves one action an adapter offered — a quick fix, an extraction, an inline, or an adapter-specific family. Arguments are validated against the schema the offer advertises. An offer carrying a portable argument contract is refused here and resolves through its own tool.

projection_restore.description: Restores changed paths from the workspace and drops the changes that touched them.

publish.description: Publishes the changeset into the workspace. A change carrying a confirmation is published only when the call accepts it, and a workspace path changed since the projection took it refuses the whole publication.

execute.description: Evaluates code against the session projection in a disposable workspace.

debug_start.description: Starts an inspect-only evaluation and retains bounded frames after a failure.

debug_get_frame.description: Reads one retained stack frame without resuming evaluation.

debug_stop.description: Releases a debugging session, adapter state, and execution workspace.

workspace.description: Reports projection state, adapter availability, limits, and hooks.

projection.description: Returns the filesystem path of this session's projection, for tools that can only work through a directory.

changes.description: Returns the changes this session has applied, each with its edits, effects, validation evidence, and the confirmations publication will check.

symbol.description: Returns one symbol and its semantic facts from the session projection.

fs.description: Returns one page of a directory's entries — subdirectories and files — or a bounded file-content range from the session projection.

actions.description: Returns the fixes and refactors an adapter offers at one address, or across one file. Each entry carries the offer identity and what the action would do, and leaves out the argument schema so a page stays bounded however many offers it holds.

action.description: Returns one discovered action with the JSON Schema of the arguments it takes. This is the read a caller makes for the offer it chose, before handing the same identity to `apply`.

rift:axes.description: Each axis owns a set of definitions. `identifiedBy` supplies its roots, then the group closes over references without taking a definition already assigned to another axis. `holds` assigns explicit definitions and `residualOf` assigns the unclaimed definitions from one schema document.

Edit.description:
A filesystem effect described before Rift performs it. Edit sets are atomic and sorted
bytewise by each edit's RFC 8785 canonical JSON.

Text replacements in one set address the same input state and cannot overlap. An empty
range at `a` overlaps `[s, e)` only when `s < a < e`, so boundary insertions are legal; two
edits sharing an insertion point apply in the set's canonical order, and an insertion at
the start of a replacement lands before the replacement text.

Application runs in phases: text replacements against the pre-state, then deletes, copies,
renames, creates, and executable-bit changes. Structural sources read the pre-state, and
two structural edits contending for one path are `invalid_request` unless a delete freed
it.

rift:enumDescriptions.adapter_protocol_error: An adapter contract is unusable. Causes include a malformed message, a field outside its range, ambiguous source or generated-source claims, overlapping write claims, a generated-path collision, and a cycle in generated-source routing. Correct the adapter configuration before retrying.
rift:enumDescriptions.adapter_timeout: The adapter took the call and did not answer inside the server's per-call budget, which is at most `max_request_ms`. Retrying can work: a cold adapter on a large workspace is slow once and fast afterwards.
rift:enumDescriptions.adapter_unavailable: A configured adapter could serve this request, but its process failed to start or died. The server restarts it on demand, doubling a one-second delay after each failed start; `retry` says `same_request` until three consecutive starts fail, then `operator_action` until the configuration changes.
rift:enumDescriptions.cancelled: The caller cancelled, or the connection went away before the request finished. Sending it again is fine.
rift:enumDescriptions.capability_unavailable: The tool exists, but the workspace configuration and configured adapters cannot serve this operation for the requested language. Read the workspace resource again after `rift.toml` or adapter availability changes.
rift:enumDescriptions.configuration_invalid: The workspace-root `rift.toml` does not satisfy its schema. New requests remain blocked until the file is valid.
rift:enumDescriptions.content_unavailable: The entry is known but its bytes cannot be read. Retrying does not help.
rift:enumDescriptions.cursor_expired: The cursor is valid, but its captured result page set left the process-local cache. Start again from the first page.
rift:enumDescriptions.cursor_invalid: The cursor is malformed, or it was minted for a different request, order or page size. Start the query again from its first page.
rift:enumDescriptions.deadline_exceeded: The request ran past `max_request_ms`. A smaller one may succeed — a lower `limit`, a narrower path selector — and so may the same one once a cold adapter has warmed up.
rift:enumDescriptions.hook_execution_failure: Rift could not launch the hook, enforce its timeout, or capture its output. One retry is reasonable when the host failure was transient.
rift:enumDescriptions.internal_error: A bug in Rift. `causes` says what it was doing at the time, and a retry is not expected to answer differently.
rift:enumDescriptions.invalid_request: The request does not satisfy the schema, or names something the schema forbids: a `limit` above the advertised maximum, a filter field that does not exist. The same bytes fail identically.
rift:enumDescriptions.limit_exceeded: A request or a response crossed an advertised limit. `limit` says which one and by how much, so the request can be resized and sent again.
rift:enumDescriptions.permission_denied: The connection cannot perform this operation: a path addresses through a symlink component, which following could take outside the workspace, or a debugging session belongs to another connection. The same request fails the same way.
rift:enumDescriptions.projection_busy: The session has an in-flight Rift FS mutation that prevents this operation. Retry after that mutation completes.
rift:enumDescriptions.resource_not_found: The identity is well-formed and resolves to nothing — no such symbol, no such filesystem entry, or a debug session already stopped or expired. Retrying does not help.
rift:enumDescriptions.storage_failure: Rift could not read or write workspace or projection files. Worth retrying only if the cause was transient, such as a disk that has since been cleared.
rift:enumDescriptions.temporarily_unavailable: The resource exists but is in use. Another connection owns the session, a retained debugger blocks continuation, a disposable workspace is still releasing, or another publication holds the workspace. Retry after that owner or operation finishes.
rift:enumDescriptions.unsupported_path: The workspace contains a path the protocol cannot represent safely.
rift:enumDescriptions.unsupported_protocol: No version the caller offered is one the server implements. `protocol` lists the versions the server supports; the caller selects one it implements and reconnects, or surfaces the mismatch.

rift:enumDescriptions.augments: `from` adds members to `to`, which is declared elsewhere — a Rust `impl` block, a TypeScript `declare module`, an `ALTER TABLE`, a CSS rule for a selector another file already styles.
rift:enumDescriptions.binds: `from` names `to` across a language boundary: a `className` and the CSS rule it selects, an ORM entity and its table.
rift:enumDescriptions.bounded_by: `from` is constrained to satisfy `to` — the `Serialize` in `T: Serialize`, the `Comparable` in `<T extends Comparable<T>>`.
rift:enumDescriptions.catches: `from` handles `to` when something it calls raises it.
rift:enumDescriptions.configures: `from` supplies configuration `to` reads — a `rift.toml` key and the field it fills, a `tsconfig` path alias and the module it resolves.
rift:enumDescriptions.contains: `from` lexically holds `to` — a module and the functions written in it.
rift:enumDescriptions.declares: `from` owns `to`. A class carries this to its methods even where the language writes them outside its body.
rift:enumDescriptions.depends_on: `from` needs `to` and there is no place in the source to point at — a manifest entry, a build dependency. The coarsest edge there is.
rift:enumDescriptions.embeds: `from` holds `to` and promotes its members, so they are reachable without naming the field. Go struct embedding.
rift:enumDescriptions.generates: `to` was produced from `from` by a build step, so editing `to` lasts until the next build.
rift:enumDescriptions.has_type: `to` is the type of `from`. What jump-to-type-definition follows.
rift:enumDescriptions.imports: `from` brings `to` in from another unit. A header or a stylesheet that declares nothing of its own is a synthetic `module` symbol, so `#include` and `@import` are the same edge as a Python `import`.
rift:enumDescriptions.instantiates: `from` applies `to` as a type argument — the `Config` in `Vec<Config>`.
rift:enumDescriptions.mixes_in: `from` takes members from `to` by linearization — a Dart `with` clause, a Scala mixin. The order they are written in decides which one wins.
rift:enumDescriptions.overloads: `from` and `to` share a name and differ in signature, and the language picks between them at the call site.
rift:enumDescriptions.reads: `from` takes the value of `to`. A SQL `SELECT` against a table is this edge.
rift:enumDescriptions.references: `from` mentions `to` somewhere in the source and nothing narrower fits. The fallback edge where there is a node to point at.
rift:enumDescriptions.specializes: `from` is a narrower form of `to`, chosen over it where both match.
rift:enumDescriptions.tests: `from` exercises `to`. A test that reaches its target through reflection or HTTP has no call edge to carry it.
rift:enumDescriptions.writes: `from` assigns to `to`. A SQL `INSERT`, `UPDATE` or `DELETE` is this edge.

capture.description: Which metavariable of the pattern this constrains, written without the `$`.

constraints.description: Conditions the captures have to meet. The pattern finds a shape; these narrow it to the intended occurrences.

rift:enumDescriptions.outermost: Keep the enclosing match. A chain of nested calls reports once, at the top.

Symbol.description: Adapter-resolved semantic identity. Source structure lives in Node and is connected through Relationship.

id.description: Unique identifier of this symbol across the whole workspace, and the URI that resolves it. Hand it to the symbol resource as it stands.

language.description: The language this symbol belongs to.

name.description: The human-readable name, as written in the source: `parseConfig`. Rendered signatures live in `signatures`.
name.title: Name

kind.description: What this symbol is in the adapter's vocabulary, such as `trait`, `function`, or `table`.

facets.description: Portable classification for cross-language queries. The local kinds `trait` and `interface` can both carry the `type` facet.
facets.title: Facets

origin.description: Where the symbol comes from: code in this workspace, or a package it depends on.

container.description: The symbol this one belongs to — the class that owns a method, the module that owns a function. Ownership is not lexical: a Go method is written beside its type and a Rust method inside an `impl` block, and both name the type here. Absent at the top level.

visibility.description: How widely the symbol is visible, in the language's own terms — `public`, `private`, `pub(crate)`. Null where the language has no such concept.
visibility.title: Visibility

types.description: The types this symbol carries, each tagged with the role it plays: a return type, a field type, a bound.
types.title: Types

signatures.description: One entry per callable form. Where the language dispatches overloads separately they are separate symbols joined by the `overloads` edge; several entries here are alternative forms of one dispatch target, as `typing.overload` writes them.
signatures.title: Signatures

documentation.description: Doc comments attached to the declaration, with the markup format they were written in.
documentation.title: Documentation

extensions.description: Language-specific facts with no portable equivalent, namespaced by the adapter that emitted them.

document_local.description: Whether language semantics confine this symbol to the document that declares it. The adapter classifies locality from its language model.
document_local.title: Document Local

Symbol.title: Symbol

SymbolFacet.description: One portable category a symbol falls into. Kinds are language-specific; facets are shared, so a filter written once applies to every language an adapter is installed for.

rift:enumDescriptions.abstract: Declared without an implementation. Whatever carries `implements` or `extends` to it has to supply one.
rift:enumDescriptions.alias: Another name for a symbol declared elsewhere — a `typealias`, a C++ `using`, a re-export. The `aliases` edge says which symbol.
rift:enumDescriptions.annotation: Declared to be attached to another declaration: a Java `@interface`, a Kotlin `annotation class`, a Python decorator, a Rust attribute macro.
rift:enumDescriptions.async: Produces a value that completes later. `Signature.effects` keeps the language's own keyword: `async`, `suspend`.
rift:enumDescriptions.callable: Can be called, and so carries at least one `Signature`.
rift:enumDescriptions.constructor: The callable that produces an instance. `constructible` marks the type it produces.
rift:enumDescriptions.deprecated: Marked as no longer to be used, however the language spells it — `@Deprecated`, `#[deprecated]`, a doc tag.
rift:enumDescriptions.entrypoint: Where execution starts: `fn main`, `func main`, a `bin` script named by the package manifest.
rift:enumDescriptions.enumeration: Declares the closed set those variants belong to. A `match` over it is exhaustive once every variant is covered.
rift:enumDescriptions.extensible: Can be inherited from or overridden: a non-`final` class, a Kotlin `open fun`, a C++ `virtual` method.
rift:enumDescriptions.extension: Attached to a type declared somewhere else — a Kotlin extension function, a method in a Rust `impl` block, a Go method, a Dart extension.
rift:enumDescriptions.generator: Yields a sequence one value at a time instead of returning once — a Python generator, a Dart `sync*` function.
rift:enumDescriptions.implementable: Names a contract another type can satisfy: an interface, a trait, a protocol.
rift:enumDescriptions.macro: Expands source at compile time, as `macro_rules!` and preprocessor definitions do.
rift:enumDescriptions.member: Owned by another symbol — a method, a field, an enum variant. Ownership is not lexical: a Go method is written beside its type, and a Rust method inside an `impl` block.
rift:enumDescriptions.member_container: Can hold members: a class, a struct, an interface.
rift:enumDescriptions.module: A unit the language imports whole. A TypeScript file carries this facet, and so do a Rust `mod` and a Go package, both of which can span several files.
rift:enumDescriptions.mutable: Can be reassigned after it is initialized. A Rust `let mut` carries it, a `let` does not.
rift:enumDescriptions.namespace: Groups names without being a unit the language loads — a C++ `namespace`, a Java package, a SQL schema.
rift:enumDescriptions.operator: Invoked through operator syntax — C++ `operator+`, Python `__add__`, a Kotlin `operator fun`.
rift:enumDescriptions.parameter: A parameter of a callable, declared as a symbol of its own so it can be renamed and referred to.
rift:enumDescriptions.property: Read and written as a value, and backed by code that runs — a Kotlin property, a Python `@property`, a JavaScript getter.
rift:enumDescriptions.public: Reachable from outside the unit that declares it. `visibility` carries the language's own word, which Go and Python do not have: there the adapter reads the naming convention.
rift:enumDescriptions.static: Bound to the declaration rather than to an instance, so a call needs no receiver.
rift:enumDescriptions.test: The language's test tooling collects it as a test: a `#[test]` function, a `describe` block.
rift:enumDescriptions.type: Declares a type. `struct Config` and `interface Props` both qualify, which is what makes one search for types find both.
rift:enumDescriptions.type_parameter: A generic parameter — the `T` in `Vec<T>`. A Rust lifetime and a C++ `template<int N>` carry it too.
rift:enumDescriptions.value: Names something that exists while the program runs: a variable, a constant, a function object. A CSS class selector and a SQL sequence carry it too.
rift:enumDescriptions.variant: One case of a closed set: a Rust enum variant, a Scala `case`, a Java enum constant.

identity from the file path, as TypeScript does, that path is part of the name. A `~N`
suffix separates declarations the qualified name alone cannot, such as overloads that
dispatch separately.

oneOf.description: Declared in this workspace's own source. Source the caller can open and change.
oneOf.title: SymbolOriginWorkspace

oneOf.description: Declared in a dependency. `manager` is the package manager that installed it, so `npm`, `cargo` or `pip`; `name` and `version` are that manager's own. Upgrading the dependency replaces these symbols.

manager.description: The package manager that installed it.
manager.title: Manager

name.description: The package name, as that manager spells it.
name.title: Name

oneOf.title: SymbolOriginPackage

oneOf.description: Declared in the language's standard library and installed with its toolchain.
oneOf.title: SymbolOriginStdlib

oneOf.description: Declared outside the workspace, its packages, and the language's standard library.
oneOf.title: SymbolOriginExternal

oneOf.description: Produced by a build step. Editing it lasts only until it is generated again.
oneOf.title: SymbolOriginGenerated

oneOf.description: Invented by the adapter, with no source declaration to read or edit.
oneOf.title: SymbolOriginSynthetic

SymbolResourcePayload.description: JSON payload for one symbol in the session projection.

uri.description: The symbol this payload answers for, echoed back so a link and its content carry the same address.

symbol.description: The declaration itself: its name, its kind in the language's own words, its origin, its types and its signatures.

origin_mappings.description: Relations from produced declaration bytes to source ranges a caller can inspect or edit. Empty for a declaration read directly from physical source.
origin_mappings.title: Origin Mappings

nodes.description: Every place this symbol is written — the declaration and each mention. This is the list a rename has to rewrite.
nodes.title: Nodes

relationships.description: Edges into and out of this symbol, each carrying the nodes from which the adapter derived it.
relationships.title: Relationships

source.description: The source at each node, so the declaration and its call sites can be read without a second round trip.
source.title: Source

diagnostics.description: What the adapter reported at this symbol's nodes.
diagnostics.title: Diagnostics

coverage.description: How complete each fact family is for this symbol. An empty `relationships` means the symbol has no edges only where that family is complete.

next.description: The same symbol URI carrying the cursor for the next page, or null on the last one. Nodes, edges and diagnostics are what page.

SymbolResourcePayload.title: SymbolResourcePayload

SymbolResourceUri.description:
URI for one symbol read. It is the symbol's own `SymbolId`, optionally carrying the
cursor that continues its paged nodes, edges, and diagnostics.
SymbolResourceUri.title: SymbolResourceUri

TextEdit.description: One byte range of one file and what replaces it. Edits in a set share one input state.

span.description: The file, and the byte range being replaced.

text.description: What the range becomes. Empty deletes it.
text.title: Text

TextEdit.title: TextEdit

TextQuery.description: Literal or regular-expression matching over any UTF-8 file. Rift evaluates this query even when no adapter claims the path. Matches are leftmost-first and non-overlapping. After an empty regular-expression match, scanning advances to the next UTF-8 boundary. The query carries its dialect so a stored match key remains self-contained.

version.description: Version of the query shape and pattern semantics.
version.title: Version

dialect.description: Regular-expression grammar used in `regex` mode. The separate `version` field selects its syntax and match semantics. Version 1 has Unicode character classes, linear-time matching, and no look-around or backreferences. Protocol conformance fixtures define accepted syntax and match selection.
dialect.title: Dialect

pattern.description: Text to find in the selected grammar.
pattern.title: Pattern

case_sensitive.description: Initial case-sensitivity for regular-expression mode. Inline flags may change it within the pattern.
case_sensitive.title: Case Sensitive

multiline.description: Whether `^` and `$` initially match line boundaries in regular-expression mode. Inline flags may change it within the pattern.
multiline.title: Multiline

TextQuery.title: TextQuery

rift:enumDescriptions.literal: Match the pattern bytewise, with no special characters or flags.
rift:enumDescriptions.regex: Read the pattern using the advertised text-matching dialect and the initial flags below.

TextRange.description: Half-open UTF-8 byte offsets over authoritative UTF-8 source. Every adapter converts from whatever its language toolchain counts in before offsets leave the adapter, so a rustc column and a tsc column arrive here on the same scale. No JSON Schema keyword can tie one field to another, so that `end` is never below `start` is asserted by the conformance tests instead.

start.description: First byte of the range, counted from the start of the file.
start.title: Start

end.description: One past the last byte. Equal to `start` for an empty range, which is how a position between two bytes is spelled.
end.title: End

TextRange.title: TextRange

TypeBinding.description: One type a symbol carries, together with the role it plays for that symbol.
TypeBinding.title: TypeBinding

TypeBindingProvenance.description: Where the type fact came from. A declared type and an inferred one can both be present and disagree, which is the interesting case.

rift:enumDescriptions.declared: Written in the source by the author.
rift:enumDescriptions.expected: What the surrounding context demands here. A mismatch is reported against this one.
rift:enumDescriptions.inferred: The adapter worked it out; nothing in the source says it.

TypeBindingProvenance.title: TypeBindingProvenance

TypeBindingRole.description: What this type is to the symbol that carries it.

rift:enumDescriptions.awaited: What completes inside an asynchronous value — the `T` in `Promise<T>`.
rift:enumDescriptions.bound: A constraint the type has to satisfy — the `Serialize` in `T: Serialize`.
rift:enumDescriptions.discriminant: The representation an enumeration is stored as, where the language pins one.
rift:enumDescriptions.element: What a container holds: the `u8` in `Vec<u8>`, the value type of a map.
rift:enumDescriptions.error: The failure type — the `E` in `Result<T, E>`, a Go `error` return.
rift:enumDescriptions.field: The type of a data member.
rift:enumDescriptions.key: The key type of a map.
rift:enumDescriptions.parameter: The type of an argument the callable takes.
rift:enumDescriptions.receiver: The type of the implicit first argument — `self`, `this`.
rift:enumDescriptions.underlying: What an alias or a newtype wraps.
rift:enumDescriptions.yielded: What a generator produces per step.

TypeBindingRole.title: TypeBindingRole

TypeExpression.description: How a type is written in the source, plus the symbol that declares it when one does. A type with a declaration resolves to that symbol; a structural type — `string | null`, `{ a: string }` — has the spelling and nothing to resolve to.

language.description: The language the spelling is in, and so the adapter that produced it.

source.description: The type as it is written: `Optional[Config]`, `&mut [u8]`, `string | null`.
source.title: Source

resolved.description: The symbol that declares this type, where one does. Null for a structural type, which has a spelling and nothing to open.

extensions.description: Type facts the model has no field for, namespaced by the adapter that emitted them.

TypeExpression.title: TypeExpression

ValidationReport.description: One adapter's verdict over a resulting tree. `coverage` states how much the adapter checked, while `valid` records whether the checked scope contains an error. `validation.require` in the workspace-root `rift.toml` decides which reports are required.

language.description: The adapter that produced this verdict.

valid.description: Whether this adapter accepted every file in `files` under the reported coverage.
valid.title: Valid

coverage.description: How much of the affected program the adapter checked. The result is incomplete when `validation.require` names this language and coverage is partial or unsupported.

files.description: Affected files this verdict covers, sorted by project path.
files.title: Files

diagnostics.description: Adapter findings produced while checking the resulting tree, sorted by file and source range.
diagnostics.title: Diagnostics

ValidationReport.title: ValidationReport

ValidationStrength.description: How much semantic validation the result contains.

rift:enumDescriptions.available: Every affected adapter that advertises validation supplied a complete report.
rift:enumDescriptions.mechanical: No affected adapter supplied a semantic validation report.
rift:enumDescriptions.required: Every language named by `validation.require` supplied a complete report.

ValidationStrength.title: ValidationStrength

WorkspacePath.description: Canonical absolute path that identifies one workspace on this host.
WorkspacePath.title: WorkspacePath

WorkspaceResourcePayload.description:
Current workspace state and request limits. Each configured language advertises its
adapter support and effective caller-code availability.

uri.description: The URI this payload answers for.

protocol_version.description: The version every other field in this payload is stated under.

limits.description: The ceilings a request has to stay inside here.

languages.description: Configured languages and their capabilities, sorted by name and dialect with null first.
languages.title: Languages

coverage.description: How complete each fact family is across the workspace. A family reported `unsupported` here remains unsupported in subsequent answers.

resources.description: The MCP resource families this workspace serves.
resources.title: Resources

next.description: The same resource carrying the cursor for the next page, or null on the last one.

matching.description: The pattern grammars the `match` tool accepts here.

hooks.description: Hooks declared by the workspace-root `rift.toml`, in execution order.
hooks.title: Hooks
